text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) summit session in its declarations has condemned Israel's expansionist designs, asked members to review relations with Israel and supported the right to self-determination of the Kashmiris.
- President Farooq Leghari asked the OIC leaders to consider setting up a permanent summit committee to mediate disputes between Moslem countries.
- Iran and Saudi Arabia have decided to settle their disputes through talks and to cooperate with each other in the larger interest of the Muslim unity, diplomatic sources said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif called upon the Islamic countries to take a united stand on the issue of weapons of mass destruction and demand their complete elimination.
- The 38 Indian children released by the Pakistan authorities were flown to Bombay on an Indian Airlines flight.

- The Privatisation Commission is confronted with the chronic problem of default on payment from well-known business groups and entrepreneurs who were awarded public sector industrial units after having been declared successful bidders.
- Pakistan's re-entry into an International Monetary Fund programme is dependent on the contents of the economic reform package and its announcement by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif is expected to chair a high-level meeting of his economic managers on March 25, to finalise proposals for a 15-month budget.
- The World Bank has shown willingness to extend financial support to the $2.5 billion 1,700-km oil pipeline from Central Asian Republics to Pakistan.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves had shot up to $1.13 billion by March 15 from the February level of $850 million.
